messages:
sophie_sales: Quick sync — NovaBank asking if our on-prem operator can do node-by-node rolling upgrades in a fully air-gapped POC and what the emergency patch pricing looks like. They want minimal disruption and audit-ready signing proof.

mark_se: TL;DR: yes for rolling upgrades, but zero user-visible downtime depends on service replicas and DB migration strategy. Operator will orchestrate cordon->drain->update->uncordon if images are available locally.

ali_eng: technical detail: we ship two bundle formats — full minibundles (all images + manifests) and delta bundles (layer diffs + manifest-mapping). For airgap we expect customers to import bundles into a local registry or preload nodes. Delta bundles save bandwidth but require stable layer digests.

ops_maya: POC hotfix option: we can offer a "POC emergency patch" add-on (48-hour response SLA) that includes triage, signed delta/minibundle build, and remote assist for import. Pricing = flat monthly surcharge on top of the POC base; exact numbers will come from sales quoting. Note: if the registry rewrites digests we either create a manifest-mapping (adds ~15–45min to import) or fall back to a full minibundle.

sophie_sales: they asked for a one-paragraph SOW snippet and a short rollback playbook for their runbook.

mark_se: SOW blurb suggestion: "Redwood will provide signed offline bundles and an operator to coordinate node-by-node rolling updates in air-gapped environments. High availability depends on replica counts for stateful services; schema-changing DB migrations may require scheduled maintenance windows. During the POC Redwood will deliver monthly security bundles and offers an optional 48-hour emergency hotfix add-on."

ali_eng: Rollback playbook (3 steps):
1) Import previous minibundle on the jumpbox: `ctr -n k8s.io images import previous-bundle.tar.gz`
2) Patch workloads to pin previous digests (or apply imagePullPolicy) and restart affected workloads: `kubectl rollout restart statefulset/<name> -n <ns>`
3) Monitor readiness (`kubectl get pods -n <ns> -w`) and if not recovering, uncordon nodes and open support ticket with Redwood SRE attaching bundle sha256 + mapping.json

ops_maya: Security questionnaire wording (short): "Bundles are produced with detached signatures (Notary v2 / cosign compatible). For POCs Redwood can sign using ephemeral keys; for production customers we support BYO KMS/HSM for signing. Verification commands and artifact checksums are provided for auditors."

mark_se: Add verification snippet they can paste into the questionnaire:
```
# on jumpbox after transfer
sha256sum bundle-2026-07-15.tar.gz > bundle.sha256
cosign verify-blob --signature bundle-2026-07-15.tar.gz.sig bundle-2026-07-15.tar.gz
ctr -n k8s.io images import bundle-2026-07-15.tar.gz
# optional preflight to detect digest rewriting
redwood-preflight --registry registry.local:5000 --check-digests
```

ali_eng: Ops caveat to include: recommend a mirrored staging cluster with identical registry behaviour to validate delta bundles and DB migrations. If they elect BYO registry that mutates digests we will include a manifest-mapping step or deliver full minibundles. Preflight typically takes 10–40 minutes.

sophie_sales: I'll email NovaBank with SOW blurb, rollback playbook, verification snippet, and ask them to confirm jumpbox + registry access, whether they want Redwood-signed POC bundles or BYO keys, and if they want the 48h hotfix add-on.

sec_bot: Recommended short answer for auditors: "Detached signatures (Notary v2). POC: Redwood ephemeral signing available. Production: BYO KMS/HSM. Verification steps and checksums provided."
